items.title: Pay invoice for wedding invitation cards
items.quote: Den Rechnungsbetrag überweisen Sie bitte binnen 14 Tagen nach dem Rechnungsdatum.
items.computation: The invoice is dated Monday 26.01.2026. The text sets the term as 'binnen 14 Tagen nach dem Rechnungsdatum'. Under § 187 Abs. 1 BGB the day of the event (26.01.2026) is not counted, so counting starts 27.01.2026; 14 days later is Monday 09.02.2026 (§ 188 Abs. 1 BGB). That day is a normal business day (no weekend/holiday shift needed under § 193 BGB), so the 14-day term as printed ends 09.02.2026. However, the invoice separately prints 'Zahlbar bis: 16.02.2026', which is 21 days after the invoice date, not 14 — the two statements on the same document contradict each other. Following the rule to use the earliest plausible reading when a letter contradicts itself, I use 09.02.2026 as the due date, with lower confidence, and flag the discrepancy.

warnings: The invoice contradicts itself on the payment deadline: the running text says 'binnen 14 Tagen nach dem Rechnungsdatum' (which computes to 09.02.2026), while the boxed line below states 'Zahlbar bis: 16.02.2026' (21 days after the invoice date) — confirm the actual due date with the sender before relying on either.

The IBAN DE64 3705 0198 0002 7270 00 is well-formed (Musterbank AG, BLZ 37050198), but a valid IBAN does not prove who owns the account; when you transfer, make sure the payee-name check (Empfängerüberprüfung) matches 'Druckerei Beispiel & Sohn' before sending, and verify the bank details against the letterhead/website you already know rather than solely this letter.
